issues.label: Sufficiency under Jackson v. Virginia
issues.why: Court must determine whether evidence viewed favorably to verdict supports malice murder beyond reasonable doubt.

issues.label: Wholly circumstantial evidence standard
issues.why: Conviction rests on circumstantial evidence, requiring exclusion of every reasonable hypothesis save guilt.

issues.label: Reasonableness of burglary hypothesis
issues.why: Court must assess whether defendant's alternative explanation of surprised burglars is a reasonable hypothesis excluding guilt.

issues.label: Proof of malice element
issues.why: Malice murder requires showing deliberate intent to kill without justification or provocation.

issues.label: Identity of shooter
issues.why: Circumstantial evidence must sufficiently identify Sheffield as the person who shot Edith.

issues.label: Motive evidence sufficiency
issues.why: The affair-based motive theory must be evaluated for its probative support of guilt.

issues.label: Barker v. Wingo balancing test
issues.why: Constitutional speedy-trial claim requires applying the four-factor balancing analysis.

issues.label: Length of delay presumptive prejudice
issues.why: Nearly six years pre-arrest plus trial delay may trigger presumptive prejudice and full analysis.

issues.label: Pre-indictment vs. post-accusation delay
issues.why: Court must determine when the speedy-trial right attached and which delay counts.

issues.label: Reasons for delay attribution
issues.why: Court must weigh whether investigative delay is attributable to the State and its weight.

issues.label: Defendant's assertion of the right
issues.why: Timing and manner of Sheffield's demand for speedy trial must be evaluated.

issues.label: Prejudice from delay
issues.why: Court must assess oppressive incarceration, anxiety, and impairment of defense including lost evidence/witnesses.

issues.label: Standard of review for speedy-trial ruling
issues.why: Appellate court must apply the abuse-of-discretion standard to the trial court's balancing.

issues.label: Admissibility/relevance of affair evidence
issues.why: Extramarital-affair and photo evidence relevance and potential prejudice may need review.

issues.label: Admission of sexual photographs
issues.why: Sexually explicit photos from old phone raise relevance and unfair-prejudice concerns.

issues.label: Post-crime conduct as evidence
issues.why: Sheffield's demeanor and failure to ask about Edith must be evaluated as consciousness-of-guilt evidence.

issues.label: Accelerant/arson inference
issues.why: Fire chief's inconclusive accelerant testimony's probative value for arson-cover-up must be assessed.

issues.label: Preservation of other claims
issues.why: Court must determine whether unspecified additional motion-for-new-trial claims were preserved and require ruling.
